actions.mechanism: Absolute expiration prevents reads from extending freshness.
actions.implementation: Assign each validated source response a monotonic expiry no later than 300 seconds after receipt. Check expiry before serving; remove expired entries and schedule expiry cleanup. Never serve expired records, including during outages.
actions.check: With a fake clock, verify a record is unavailable at its expiry boundary and repeated reads do not extend its lifetime.
actions.risk: Process-local monotonic timestamps cannot be reused after a restart.

actions.action: Define timeout responses and outage eviction explicitly.
actions.mechanism: Bounded source calls separate unavailable data from missing records.
actions.implementation: Set a configurable source deadline. Return 504 when it expires and 503 for source unavailability. Do not cache either failure. Existing unexpired records remain usable until their original expiry; failures neither extend their lifetime nor flush them. Delete expired records normally.
actions.check: Simulate an outage across an expiry boundary: a pre-expiry hit succeeds, a post-expiry request fails explicitly, and the expired entry is removed.
actions.risk: Clients may retry aggressively; document retry behavior.

actions.mechanism: A bounded cache with least-recently-used eviction controls capacity independently of source health.
actions.implementation: Under one cache lock, replace an existing key or remove expired entries and evict the least-recently-used entry before inserting a new key. Failed fetches never evict valid entries. Keep no secondary cache of evicted records.
actions.check: Insert 101 distinct records and race concurrent insertions; assert resident record count never exceeds 100 and the expected victim disappears.
actions.risk: A scan of many distinct keys can evict frequently useful records.

actions.action: Coalesce concurrent misses and bound outstanding fetches.
actions.mechanism: Single-flight fetching prevents duplicate work; admission limits bound temporary record residency.
actions.implementation: Maintain one in-flight promise per key. Reserve a record slot before starting each distinct fetch, counting reservations plus cached records against 100. Reject new misses with 503 when no slot is available. Release reservations on every completion path; do not retain response copies in the promise registry.
actions.check: Send concurrent requests for one key and then many distinct keys; assert one fetch per key and cached records plus reservations never exceed 100.
actions.risk: Conservative reservations can reject misses even when some cached entries could be evicted.

actions.action: Stop repeatedly calling a failing source.
actions.mechanism: A circuit breaker provides fail-fast outage behavior without changing cache freshness.
actions.implementation: After a configured number of consecutive source failures, open the circuit for a configured cooldown. Continue serving only unexpired hits; return 503 for misses. Permit one recovery probe after cooldown. Preserve normal expiration and eviction while open.
actions.check: Force the failure threshold, verify subsequent misses make no source calls, then confirm one successful probe closes the circuit without reviving expired records.
actions.risk: An overly long cooldown delays recognition of recovery.

actions.action: Restrict the service to explicitly public records.
actions.mechanism: Allowlisted sources, request forms, and response fields prevent private-data admission.
actions.implementation: Fetch only approved public endpoints without user credentials. Reject private-resource selectors and authorization-bearing requests. Validate response schemas and cache only allowlisted public fields. Exclude record bodies and sensitive request values from logs, traces, and errors.
actions.check: Test forbidden endpoints, credential-bearing requests, and unexpected response fields; verify rejection and absence of their contents from cache and telemetry.
actions.risk: Schema checks alone cannot establish that a source remains public; source classification needs review.
